extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, and students learning Macaulay2 for algebraic geometry and commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory documentation for using Macaulay2: shows a first example (computing a minimal free resolution), commands for getting help, pointers to learning resources, development and contribution guidance, and recommended editor setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute minimal free resolution (example workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example sequence to compute the minimal free resolution of the twisted cubic using Macaulay2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Code sequence shown: R = QQ[x, y, z, w]; -- defines a ring
I = monomialCurveIdeal(R, {1, 2, 3})
C = res I -- computes the resolution
betti I -- displays the Betti table
The page shows the resulting ideal, chain complex (resolution), and Betti tally outputs as concrete examples of expected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting help via interactive commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways to get quick usage, detailed examples, and documentation from within Macaulay2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '? monomialCurveIdeal' for quick usage information; 'help monomialCurveIdeal' for details and examples; 'viewHelp monomialCurveIdeal' for documentation on the web; 'headlines about "curve"' for documentation headlines. Also suggested help topics to try: help "reading the documentation", help "getting help or reporting bugs", help "Tutorial: Modules in Macaulay2", help "computing Groebner bases".

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain/run Macaulay2 (installation and online trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options for getting and trying Macaulay2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download Macaulay2 or 'Try M2 in a Browser' — the site provides both installation downloads and an in-browser trial option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn by reading (primary learning resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended written resources for learning Macaulay2 and computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed resources include: Getting Started, Computations Book, Documentation, Language Reference, Internal Notes, Source Code. These are presented as primary reading material for users to learn features and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn by writing (hands-on / development resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pathways for learning by creating code, sessions, and packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested items include: 'A first Macaulay2 session', Project Ideas, Package Development, M2 Style Guide, Package directory. These guide new users toward practical, project-based learning and package creation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: M2 Style Guide (coding/style guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A named resource indicating there is a style guide for writing Macaulay2 packages and code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'M2 Style Guide' among development resources — implies there are recommended conventions and style rules for package development (linking to the style guide for specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation hierarchy and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of documentation types available for different user needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is organized into: Documentation (general), Language Reference (language specifics), Internal Notes (developer/internal details), and Source Code (authoritative reference). Users are guided to consult the appropriate level depending on their needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended IDE/editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred editor for Macaulay2 use in research and available community plugins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended IDE for using Macaulay2 in research is Emacs. Community plugins are also available for Vim, Atom, VSCode, and Sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and contribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: How to engage with the Macaulay2 community, report bugs, and contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bug reports and contributions are welcome on GitHub. Community interaction is via Events & Community pages, Workshops, Slack Workspace, and Google Groups. The page identifies the site author (Mahrud Sayrafi) and that the site is a personal project, encouraging community contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: M2 for research and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Macaulay2 in research contexts and avenues for community learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections such as 'M2 for Research' and 'JSAG' as well as 'Workshops' indicate that Macaulay2 is positioned for research use and that workshops and events are available for training and community engagement.
